The scattering of light by particles much smaller than its wavelength, such as the nitrogen and oxygen molecules in air, named after Lord Rayleigh.

## Shorter wavelengths scatter more

The strength of the scattering goes with the inverse fourth power of the wavelength, so blue light near 450 nm scatters about four times as strongly as red light near 700 nm. Light scattered out of sunlight reaches the eye from every direction of the sky, and most of it is blue.

## Why not violet

Violet scatters even more, but sunlight carries less of it, some is absorbed high in the atmosphere, and human eyes are less sensitive to it.

## Sunsets

At sunset the light crosses much more air. Most of the blue has been scattered away before it arrives, leaving the reds and oranges.

## What I said reading it

I had always heard the answer as "the sky reflects the sea". It does not.
